bridge_line: The first Roman emperor to back the Christians. He ruled from 306 to 337.
A bishop and historian. He wrote the emperor's life years after the events.
A Christian writer whose account of the same battle was written earlier, and differs.
Bishop of Milan, who refused to hand a church over to the emperor's court.
He wrote the life of Ambrose, about twenty years after Ambrose died.
A bishop of Rome. His letter of 341 is our earliest claim of Rome's standing.
A bishop of Rome. His letter on Christ's two natures was read at Chalcedon.
A bishop of Rome who filled the city with inscriptions honouring the martyrs.
An Alexandrian bishop. We have Julius's letter only because he copied it out.

bridge_line: A young man in Milan at the time. He later wrote of the vigil he saw kept for Ambrose.
